tsa-a02-v01.inference: The means-less itself is announced first: exposition promised.
premises: Now the means-less itself, first of all.
tsa-a02-v01.question: What comes first, and what is promised?
tsa-a02-v01.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, promising)

tsa-a02-v02.inference: The struck one's immersion is means-devoid and ever-risen.
premises: Pierced by firm descent of power, discriminating of oneself, teacher's word heeded but once.
tsa-a02-v02.question: Whose immersion needs no means?
tsa-a02-v02.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, describing)

tsa-a02-v03.inference: Every use of means is void: nothing to attain, notify, unveil, or enter — all is Śiva already.
premises: Reasoning itself is yoga's limb — but how discern at all?
This Lord, self-light-natured, is own self: what could means do?
No notifying — self-luminous manifestation needs none.
No veil-removal — no covering of any kind exists.
No entering the non-entered — enterer and entered not distinct.
tsa-a02-v03.question: What can means accomplish?
tsa-a02-v03.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, reasoning)

tsa-a02-v04.inference: I am That; the universe mirrors in me; immersion is ever-present and means-less.
premises: What means here? Of it too, as distinct — impossible.
Hence all this is one consciousness-only reality: unmeasured, unbounded, unfaded, uncontrolled, unindicated, unelaborated.
By own will alone: autonomous, bliss-dense reality.
That am I; therein, within me, the universe reflected.
For one firmly discerning, ever: Lordly immersion, means-less itself.
For it no constraint at all — by mantra, worship, meditation, conduct.
tsa-a02-v04.question: Who am I, and what need of means?
tsa-a02-v04.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, concluding)

tsa-a02-v01.plain_english: First of the four ways in: the way with no way. We shall expound it.

tsa-a02-v02.plain_english: When grace has struck firm, a person hears the teacher's word once — and then discriminates for himself. From that point his immersion needs nothing and never sets.
tsa-a02-v02.sanskrit_cite: yadā khalu dṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhaḥ svayam eva itthaṃ vivecayati sakṛd eva guruvacanam avadhārya tadā punar upāyavirahito nityoditaḥ asya samāveśaḥ

tsa-a02-v03.plain_english: Here "yoga-limb" means one thing only: thinking it through. But what is there to think? The Lord, who is self-shining, is yourself. So what could a means do? It can't get you your nature — you have it eternally. It can't inform you — you shine already. It can't strip a covering — there is none. It can't take you inside — there's no outsider to go in.
tsa-a02-v03.sanskrit_cite: atra ca tarka eva yogāṅgam iti kathaṃ vivecayati iti cet ucyate yo 'yaṃ parameśvaraḥ svaprakāśarūpaḥ svātmā tatra kim upāyena kriyate na svarūpalābho nityatvāt na jñaptiḥ svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt nāvaraṇavigamaḥ āvaraṇasya kasyacid api asaṃbhavāt na tadanupraveśaḥ anupraveṣṭuḥ vyatiriktasya abhāvāt

tsa-a02-v04.plain_english: And the means itself, as something separate from you, is equally impossible. So: all this is one reality, consciousness and nothing else — time can't measure it, place can't bound it, qualities can't fade it, shapes can't rule it, words can't point it out, proofs can't build it up. By its own will it is what lets everything from time to proof arrive at its nature; free, thick bliss; and that is I, with the universe mirrored inside me. Who sees this steadily is immersed in the Lord always, without means — no mantra binds him, no worship, no sitting, no observance.
tsa-a02-v04.sanskrit_cite: kaś cātra upāyaḥ tasyāpi vyatiriktasya anupapatteḥ tasmāt samastam idam ekaṃ cinmātratattvaṃ kālena akalitaṃ deśena aparicchinnam upādhibhir amlānam ākṛtibhir aniyantritaṃ śabdair asaṃdiṣṭaṃ pramāṇair aprapañcitaṃ kālādeḥ pramāṇaparyantasya svecchayaiva svarūpalābhanimittaṃ ca svatantram ānandaghanaṃ tattvaṃ tad eva ca aham tatraiva antar mayi viśvaṃ pratibimbitam evaṃ dṛḍhaṃ viviñcānasya śaśvad eva pārameśvaraḥ samāveśo nirupāyaka eva tasya ca na mantrapūjādhyānacaryādiniyantraṇā kācit

essence: The way with no way: when grace has struck firm, one word from the teacher and the immersion is ever-risen — no means required.
Four impossibilities: no nature to attain, nothing to notify, no covering to remove, no one to enter; the means itself impossible.
All is one consciousness-only reality — unmeasured, unbounded, unfaded, uncontrolled, unindicated, unelaborated — autonomous, bliss-dense; I am that, with the universe mirrored in me.
No mantra, worship, meditation, or conduct binds one who sees this steadily.

rasa.justification: Immediate recognition (anupāya) as wonder settling into taught peace: the four impossibilities end in identity.
